title: Granada grows over 2,700 years
episode: Granada: 2,700 Years in 12 Minutes | 3D Timelapse (700 BC–2025)
description: A 3D animated map of Granada growing from an Iberian settlement on the Albaicín hill to a Roman town, the capital of a Muslim kingdom, and the modern city. San Nicolás, on the same hill, has the classic view of the Alhambra.

title: The Alhambra explained
description: A clear, well-illustrated history of the Alhambra: how the Nasrid dynasty built a palace city on a hill above Granada in the 1200s and 1300s, and what its tilework, carved plaster, and fountains were meant to say.

title: Passages under the palace
episode: The hidden world beneath the ancient Alhambra fortress - BBC REEL
description: A short BBC film on the Alhambra’s hidden side: tunnels and passages beneath the palace, and the defenses of towers like the Comares Tower, which holds the throne room of the Nasrid sultans.

title: How Spain was reconquered
episode: How did the Reconquista Actually Happen? - Explained in 11 Minutes
description: An animated summary of the Reconquista, the Christian kingdoms’ slow advance south through Muslim Spain, which ended when Granada surrendered in January 1492. Its conquerors, Isabella and Ferdinand, are buried in the Royal Chapel.

title: The decree that expelled the Jews
description: Months after taking Granada, Isabella and Ferdinand signed a decree in the Alhambra ordering all Jews to convert or leave Spain. This explains the century of persecution behind it. The Realejo, below the Alhambra, was the Jewish quarter.

title: Hollywood in the caves
episode: The Small World: "The Gypsy Children of Granada" (1963)
description: An unsold 1963 American TV pilot, directed by the Hollywood cinematographer James Wong Howe, about the Romani children and families who lived in the cave houses of Sacromonte, the hill across from the Alhambra.

title: Flamenco in a cave
episode: Flamenco Zambra @ Sacromonte, Granada - Los Tarantos
description: A full zambra, the Romani wedding dance of Sacromonte, filmed in a whitewashed cave with the audience a few feet from the dancers. The caves have been staging these shows for visitors since the 1800s.

title: An American poet reads Lorca
episode: Philip Levine reads Federico Garcia Lorca | LIVE from the NYPL
description: Philip Levine, a former American poet laureate, reads Lorca in English and talks about what the Granada poet meant to him. Lorca wrote many of his best-known works at his family’s summer house here.

title: Holy Week processions
episode: Semana Santa (Holy Week) - Easter Processions in Granada, Spain
description: Easter week in Granada, when religious brotherhoods carry heavy floats of the Virgin and Christ through the streets to the cathedral, accompanied by brass bands and hooded penitents.

title: Free tapas
description: A food writer living in Spain makes a round of Granada’s bars, where a free tapa still comes with every drink and each round brings something different. Calle Navas, near the town hall, is lined with tapas bars.
